stem: So great _____ the demand that the course was offered twice.
explanation: Fronting "So + adjective" triggers inversion of the verb and subject: So great was the demand that...

stem: Were the government _____ the tax, prices would rise sharply.
explanation: "Were + subject + to-infinitive" is a formal inverted conditional for a hypothetical future event.

stem: Take notes carefully _____ you forget the key arguments.
explanation: "Lest" (formal) means "so that ... not" or "for fear that".

stem: The theory is useful _____ it explains the observed variation.
explanation: "Insofar as" means "to the extent that".

stem: _____ the objections of several members, the proposal was approved.
explanation: "Notwithstanding" is a formal preposition meaning "despite" and is followed by a noun phrase.

stem: Her _____ the deadline surprised everyone on the team.
explanation: After a possessive (Her), a gerund acts as the noun: Her missing the deadline surprised everyone.

stem: None of the evidence _____ the author's central claim.
explanation: With an uncountable noun (evidence), "none of" takes a singular verb: supports.

stem: The researchers claim _____ on the problem for over a decade.
explanation: The perfect continuous infinitive (to have been working) describes an activity continuing up to the time of the claim.

stem: _____ been warned about the risks, the investors withdrew their funds.
explanation: A perfect participle clause (Having been warned) shows a completed passive action before the main clause.

stem: The speaker finished her talk, _____ the audience rose to applaud.
explanation: "Whereupon" means "immediately after which".

stem: It could be argued that the policy _____ more harm than good.
explanation: The collocation is "do more harm than good"; the present perfect links the policy's effects to the present.

stem: Such _____ the complexity of the issue that no simple solution exists.
explanation: "Such is/was + noun phrase + that" is an inverted emphatic structure.

stem: The findings are _____ inconclusive to justify a change in policy.
explanation: "Too + adjective + to-infinitive" means the degree prevents the result.

stem: Only by comparing both datasets _____ the discrepancy.
explanation: "Only by + -ing" at the beginning triggers subject–auxiliary inversion: could we identify.

stem: It is high time the university _____ its admissions policy.
explanation: "It's (high) time + subject" is followed by the past simple with present meaning.

stem: I would rather _____ the conference than presented a poorly prepared paper.
explanation: "Would rather have + past participle" expresses a preference about the past, matching "presented".

stem: She might well _____ the prize had she submitted her work on time.
explanation: The inverted third conditional (had she submitted) requires a past modal result: might well have won.

stem: The proposal is both innovative and _____.
explanation: "Both ... and" must link elements of the same form: two adjectives (innovative and practical).

stem: The author seeks not merely to describe the problem but _____ it.
explanation: "Not merely to X but to Y" requires parallel infinitives.

stem: _____ the study's limitations, its conclusions remain broadly valid.
explanation: "For all" + noun phrase means "despite".

stem: The professor, _____ the students had great respect, retired last year.
explanation: The verb phrase is "have respect for", so the preposition moves before the relative pronoun: for whom.

stem: The results, _____ are discussed below, challenge earlier assumptions.
explanation: "The implications of which" is a formal relative structure meaning "whose implications".

stem: _____ the evidence may be, the court must reach a decision.
explanation: "However + adjective + subject + may be" means "no matter how".

stem: Scarcely _____ the results been published when critics attacked the methodology.
explanation: "Scarcely had + subject + past participle ... when" describes one past event immediately followed by another.

stem: The committee demanded that the report _____ immediately.
explanation: After verbs of demand and recommendation, formal English uses the subjunctive: be withdrawn.

stem: The author's argument, _____ persuasive, overlooks several counterexamples.
explanation: "While + adjective" is a reduced concessive clause meaning "although it is".

stem: Rarely, if _____, do such anomalies appear in the data.
explanation: The fixed expression is "rarely, if ever".

stem: The data, _____ collected over five years, provide a detailed picture.
explanation: "Having been collected" is a perfect passive participle modifying "the data".

stem: The phenomenon, _____ first observed in the 1970s, remains poorly understood.
explanation: "Though + participle" is a reduced concessive clause: though (it was) first observed.

stem: Few, if _____, of the participants completed every task.
explanation: The fixed expression is "few, if any".

stem: There is _____ evidence to support the claim that the drug is harmful.
explanation: "Evidence" is uncountable, so "little" (not "few") is used to mean "not much".

stem: _____ an expert in the field, she was consulted on the new legislation.
explanation: A present participle clause (Being an expert) gives the reason for the main action.

stem: The more data we collect, _____ our predictions become.
explanation: The comparative correlative requires "the" in both parts: The more..., the more accurate...

stem: This method is no _____ effective than the traditional one.
explanation: "No more + adjective + than" means "not at all more ... than".

stem: The later model consumes _____ energy than its predecessor.
explanation: "Energy" is uncountable, so "less" is used; the adverb "considerably" modifies the comparative.

stem: It is the students themselves _____ must take responsibility for their learning.
explanation: In the cleft structure "It is X who...", "who" is the subject of "must take".

stem: All _____ remains is to write the conclusion.
explanation: After "all", the relative pronoun "that" is used (not "what"): All that remains...

stem: The lecturer spoke as though she _____ the topic for years.
explanation: "As though" describing an unreal or uncertain past situation uses the past perfect (continuous).

stem: The article, _____ to have been written in haste, contains several errors.
explanation: A present participle (appearing) forms a reduced relative clause: which appears to have been written in haste.

stem: _____ as it may seem, the simplest explanation is often the correct one.
explanation: The concessive pattern "Adjective + as + subject + may seem" means "although it may seem adjective".

stem: The board has yet _____ a final decision.
explanation: "Have yet + to-infinitive" means something has not happened so far.

stem: The paper is concerned _____ the ethical dimensions of genetic research.
explanation: "Be concerned with" means "be about / deal with" in academic writing.

stem: _____ the survey results, customer satisfaction has declined steadily.
explanation: "Judging by/from" is a fixed participle expression meaning "based on".

stem: The distinction between the two terms is _____ subtle to matter in practice.
explanation: "Too + adjective + to-infinitive" expresses that something exceeds the degree needed for a result.

stem: The criteria _____ in the appendix.
explanation: "Criteria" is the plural of "criterion", so it takes a plural verb.

stem: The phenomena described in the report _____ well documented.
explanation: "Phenomena" is the plural of "phenomenon", so the verb is plural: are.

stem: _____ it is often claimed, bilingualism does not delay language development.
explanation: "Contrary to what + clause" introduces a claim that is being rejected.

stem: The treaty was signed in 1648, _____ the war finally came to an end.
explanation: "At which point" is a relative expression meaning "and at that moment".

stem: _____ the professor's absence, the seminar was led by a graduate student.
explanation: "Owing to" + noun phrase gives a reason; "because" and "since" require a clause.

stem: Whether the policy succeeds _____ largely on public support.
explanation: A clause (Whether the policy succeeds) acting as the subject takes a singular verb: depends.

stem: The author's _____ of the period is remarkably detailed.
explanation: A possessive (the author's) is followed by a noun: depiction.

stem: The theory is _____ flawed, since it ignores several key variables.
explanation: An adjective (flawed) is modified by an adverb: fundamentally.
